title: The Death of Developer Advocates — Stephanie Jarmak, Sourcegraph
talk_summary: A Sourcegraph research scientist argues DevRel must now serve agents as users, and describes two concrete mechanisms: a benchmark (CodeScaleBench) that runs agents with/without their MCP tool to find friction in tool schemas, and a GEO experiment measuring whether chatbots recommend their product. The transferable core is instrumenting agent tool-use traces to find wasted turns and fixing tool descriptions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run agents on many SDLC tasks with and without the tool, collect thousands of traces, and inspect failing turns to find where the model's training-data bias clashes with the tool's parameter names or descriptions, then fix the description/schema.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it tried to use like read line instead of start line or something like that... it's burning right an entire turn just failing. And you could just go in and fix that

takeaways.technique: A/B benchmark of tooling with vs without
takeaways.what_they_do: Built hundreds of tasks reflecting the software dev lifecycle and ran agents with and without their product tooling to quantify whether the tool helps and where it breaks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I developed hundreds of tasks that were reflective of the software development life cycle. And I basically unleashed these agents with and without um our product tooling.
takeaways.numbers: hundreds of tasks; thousands of traces

takeaways.what_they_do: Point a coding agent at your docs, read the transcript, and turn observed confusion into an 'agent experience report' / rubric for how agents encounter your content and interfaces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: point a coding agent at your docs, and then looking through that transcript and start developing your agent experience report

takeaways.what_they_do: Publish llms.txt-style authoritative pages, keep examples current, prefer structured content (charts, FAQs, explicit pain/use-case mapping) because agents quote and re-rank it; agents tolerate structured 'slop' humans dislike.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they still need to be using the tools and using real-time information and provenance... you also want to give like the agent something to quote

takeaways.technique: Spin up many agents for experiments humans won't do
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses fleets of agents to run experiments (benchmarks, GEO prompt sweeps) at a scale impractical with human developers, then feeds results back to product/marketing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also uh basically spin up like thousands of these agents to perform experiments on them
